entries.summary: Something you believe about your customers but have not checked. A guess can feel like knowing, right up until a customer proves it wrong.
entries.tip: Watch what people actually ask for, and buy for them.
evidence: Day {day}: {totalAsked} customers came. Most asked for {mostAskedItem} ({mostAskedCount}).

sources.title: The Lean Startup
sources.author: Eric Ries
sources.idea: A business plan starts as a set of assumptions that are often wrong, so the first job is to test them quickly.

sources.title: The Mom Test
sources.author: Rob Fitzpatrick
sources.idea: What customers have actually done tells you more than their opinions or what they say they will do.

entries.summary: Revenue is all the money that comes in from sales. Profit is what is left after you pay for the goods you sold. Margin is the share of each sale that you keep.
entries.tip: Look at what you keep, not what you take in.
evidence: Day {day}: you took {revenueToday} in sales, and after paying for the goods you kept {profitToday}.

sources.title: Revenue vs. profit: why the differences matter for small businesses
sources.author: Chase for Business
sources.idea: Revenue is what comes in from sales, while profit is what remains once costs are taken out.

sources.title: Margin vs. markup
sources.author: Xero
sources.idea: Margin describes how much of a selling price is profit, and is not the same thing as markup.

sources.title: Revenue vs. profit: what businesses need to know
sources.author: Start Up Loans
sources.idea: Looking at sales alone can hide how little a business is actually keeping.

entries.summary: When you raise a price, fewer people buy. When you lower it, more people buy, but you keep less from each sale. How much it matters differs from one product to another.
entries.tip: Change one price at a time, and watch who walks away.

evidence.text: Day {day}: {pricedPeople} walked away over your price for {pricedItem}.
Day {day}: nobody walked away over your prices.

sources.title: Understanding Price Elasticity: How It Affects Your Business Strategy
sources.author: Small Business Trends
sources.idea: Price elasticity of demand measures how much the amount people buy changes when the price changes.

sources.title: Price elasticity in the real world: how sensitive customers really are
sources.author: Business Initiative
sources.idea: Testing different prices with real customers shows how sensitive they are, which is often less than owners expect.
